A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OmniArch research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable matching despite reformatting, additions, and removal of the v2 checklist.

before.justification: v2 reports original PDE prediction experiments, zero-shot evaluations, inverse-problem results, loss ablations, and inference measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds masking and PDE-Aligner controls, additional baseline results, and a finite-difference solver comparison.

M1.justification: The Fourier encoder/decoder, shared Transformer, Temporal Mask, PDE-Aligner, and pre-training/fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. Expanded explanations and revised normalization documentation do not establish a procedural change; squared-norm stabilization was already described in v2 Appendix G.

E1.justification: v3 Appendix H.8 and Table 19 add a 2D-advection evaluation, whereas the earlier advection benchmark was one-dimensional. The existing PDEBench/PDEArena coverage, zero-shot scenarios, and inverse problems remain. The Well is newly cited but is not reported as an evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Poseidon-L on 2D CFD, reaction-diffusion, and SWE, and DPOT-L on those tasks plus 3D CFD. Table 19 introduces an FDM comparator. These substantially broaden comparison with contemporary pretrained models and traditional numerical solving; the earlier evaluated baselines remain.

E3.justification: v3 adds causal/no-mask controls, fine-tuning without PDE-Aligner, and an eight-resolution FDM timing and relative-error comparison from 64×64 to 512×512. Appendix A revises the stated normalization from variance to squared L2 norm plus epsilon, although v2 Appendix G already described norm stabilization. Retained splits and training settings are unchanged; rerunning earlier experiments is not established.

E4.justification: New Table 2 directly tests Temporal Mask against causal and unrestricted attention on three multi-physics tasks. Table 3 adds ordinary fine-tuning without PDE-Aligner, separating alignment benefits from fine-tuning generally; its pre-training and aligned averages summarize retained results. These address central component-attribution questions beyond the retained loss-function ablation and existing robustness analyses.

E5.justification: The standard-deviation row, inverse-problem ± values, and plotted error bars are retained. However, removing the checklist also removes v2's explicit statement that main results average repeated experiments and report standard deviations. Neither version specifies numerical run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: Most matched scores remain unchanged, but v3 adds substantial baseline, ablation, and efficiency results. DPOT-L's new 2D-CFD score of 0.0112 beats unchanged fine-tuned OmniArch-L at 0.0125, replacing v2's 29.70% improvement entry with a dash. Table 19 newly reports speedups from 0.048× to 155.4×. The added claim of 4–7× zero-shot error reduction exceeds the approximately 1.5–4.8× ratios supported by unchanged Table 4.

T1.justification: The notation table changes sigma_u from physical-field variance in v2 Table 4 to squared L2 norm plus epsilon in v3 Table 6. This is a limited revision of a mathematical definition, partly reconciling existing Appendix G documentation. The principal equations and equation-augmentation examples remain, with no new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims: unified 1D–2D–3D pre-training, flexible grids and physical quantities, PDE-Aligner supervision, benchmark superiority, and zero-shot/in-context capabilities. Added supporting experiments do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations concerning coupled-variable attention, spectral phase and energy signatures, Parseval's theorem, dimension-independent alignment, intrinsic physical resolution, and transferable operators. Appendices E.3 and H.8 add parameter-efficiency interpretations and an efficiency–interpretability tradeoff. Some interpretations exceed the evidence, including the claimed optimal intermediate resolution in Figure 4. Appendix B's original limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Tables 11–12 newly disclose component-level and task-active parameter counts, and Section 4.1 identifies large pretrained Poseidon/DPOT checkpoints. Existing hyperparameters, hardware information, and the model-access link remain. Checklist removal drops explicit statements about supplementary code, running scripts, and licensing, without establishing that those resources became unavailable.

R1.justification: v3 adds contemporary PDE foundation-model references, Poseidon/DPOT discussion, and The Well citation. New Appendix I briefly contrasts scaling and in-context learning with cited meta-learning approaches and suggests combining them. This extends research context while retaining the original novelty positioning and most related-work discussion.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes concentrate on expanded method explanations and result interpretations, revised title/affiliation text, added acknowledgements and impact statement, supplementary contents and discussion, and removal of the checklist. The narrative is extended rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, extensively resizing and relocating displays. Figure 1 is redesigned from a per-PDE radar plot into a dimensionality summary with conceptual illustrations. Five tables are added and Table 1 gains baseline rows. v3's main confusion matrix redisplays v2 Appendix Figure 8; most other figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new masking and ordinary-fine-tuning controls improve attribution of benefits to core components, while Poseidon/DPOT comparisons make the evaluation more informative. These provide a limited net improvement over v2. The gain is constrained by missing FDM implementation and timing details, reduced repeated-experiment documentation, and new overstatements, notably the claimed 4–7× zero-shot reduction despite Table 4 supporting approximately 1.5–4.8×.
